channel.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
channel.description: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

item.title: What to know about the wacky first 5 weeks of the NFL season
item.description: It's been a topsy turvy NFL season so far. We check in with Jason Gay from The Wall Street Journal about what has surprised him after five weeks of football.

item.title: Rise in accidents involving kids and e-bikes sparks debate about regulation
item.description: Emergency room departments are reporting soaring numbers of pediatric trauma accidents associated with micromobility devices. Experts and advocates agree that the federal government needs to step in.
item.content:encoded: Emergency room departments are reporting soaring numbers of pediatric trauma accidents associated with micromobility devices. Experts and advocates agree that the federal government needs to step in.

item.title: Remains of 11 Native children who died at a boarding school are returned to tribes
item.description: The Office of Army Cemeteries have returned the remains of 11 Native American and Alaska Native students who died while attending the Carlisle boarding school in Pennsylvania more than a century ago.
item.content:encoded: The Office of Army Cemeteries have returned the remains of 11 Native American and Alaska Native students who died while attending the Carlisle boarding school in Pennsylvania more than a century ago.

item.title: A Korean city borrows an educational model from the U.S. amid AI concerns
item.description: Some South Korean schools have imported a U.S. educational model to boost literacy skills and independent thinking eroded by AI and a test-focused Korean educational system.

item.title: Trump announced a partial Russia-Ukraine ceasefire. Did either country know about it?
item.description: Ukraine's leader says Russia is continuing to attack Ukraine and is ignoring an "energy ceasefire" declared by President Trump.

item.title: Oil-heated households in Northeast strained by rising fuel prices
item.description: Rising fuel prices are stressing household budgets in the Northeast, where many rely on heating oil to warm their homes.

item.title: Sauna research gathers steam
item.description: Leading researchers in heat exposure are coming together to reach a consensus on what we know — and don't — about the health benefits of sauna and its potential for treating and preventing disease.

item.title: Many Iranians who go to Turkey to find jobs are exploited
item.description: Desperate Iranians are finding work in Turkey to make ends meet, but many are being exploited and left with nothing but more debt.

item.title: Farmers say they'll take the relief of Trump's EO — but they're still hurting
item.description: President Trump says his Monday executive order temporarily suspending federal taxes on diesel will be a big relief for farmers. Some farmers call it a campaign ploy with marginal impact.
